title: गैरदलीय स्थानीय तहको माग लिएर निर्वाचन आयोग पुगे ऋषि धमला
content:
No ads found for this position काठमाडौं । स्वतन्त्र नागरिक अभियान, नेपालले आगामी स्थानीय तहको निर्वाचन गैरदलीय (ननपार्टिजन) प्रणालीबाट गर्न माग गरेको छ । अभियानले स्थानीय तहको निर्वाचन प्रणाली सुधार तथा सर्वदलीय राजनीतिक संवादमा नागरिक समाजको संस्थागत प्रतिनिधित्व सुनिश्चित गर्न माग गर्दै निर्वाचन आयोगसमक्ष ज्ञापनपत्र बुझाएको छ। अभियानका अध्यक्ष एवं संयोजक ऋषि धमलाको नेतृत्वमा आयोग पुगेको टोलीले स्थानीय तहलाई दलीय राजनीतिक हस्तक्षेपबाट मुक्त राख्दै जनमुखी, पारदर्शी र जवाफदेही शासन व्यवस्था स्थापित गर्न गैरदलीय निर्वाचन प्रणाली आवश्यक रहेको जनाएको छ। अभियानले स्थानीय तहमा बढ्दो दलीयकरण, राजनीतिक ध्रुवीकरण, भागबन्डा र बजेट विनियोजनमा देखिएका समस्या तथा सार्वजनिक सेवा प्रवाह र वित्तीय अनुशासनमा देखिएको विचलनले स्थानीय शासनको प्रभावकारितामा असर पारेको उल्लेख गरेको छ। ज्ञापनपत्रमा स्थानीय तहको निर्वाचन गैरदलीय प्रणालीबाट सम्पन्न गर्न आवश्यक संवैधानिक तथा कानुनी व्यवस्था मिलाउन सरकारलाई सिफारिस गर्न आयोगसँग आग्रह गरिएको छ। त्यस्तै, स्थानीय तहको निर्वाचनमा राजनीतिक दलको चुनाव चिह्नको सट्टा स्वतन्त्र निर्वाचन चिह्नको व्यवस्था गरी उम्मेदवारलाई स्वतन्त्र रूपमा प्रतिस्पर्धा गर्ने वातावरण बनाउन माग गरिएको छ। अभियानले निर्वाचन प्रणाली सुधार, आधारसंहिता निर्माण, कानुन संशोधन तथा स्थानीय तहको निर्वाचनसम्बन्धी विषयमा आयोजना हुने सर्वदलीय राजनीतिक सभा, परामर्श, छलफल र नीतिगत बहसमा स्वतन्त्र नागरिक अभियानको आधिकारिक तथा संस्थागत प्रतिनिधित्व सुनिश्चित गर्नुपर्ने मागसमेत गरेको छ। त्यसैगरी, गैरदलीय स्थानीय तह निर्वाचनका लागि आवश्यक कानुनी तथा प्रशासनिक आधार तय गरेर आगामी स्थानीय तहको निर्वाचनको मिति घोषणा गर्न पनि अभियानले आग्रह गरेको छ। नेपालको संविधान २०७२ ले स्थानीय तहलाई स्थानीय स्वायत्तता, जनसहभागिता र प्रत्यक्ष जनउत्तरदायित्वको आधारमा सञ्चालन गर्ने परिकल्पना गरेको उल्लेख गर्दै अभियानले स्थानीय तहलाई दलगत हस्तक्षेपबाट मुक्त राख्नुपर्नेमा जोड दिएको छ। अभियानले निर्वाचन प्रणाली सुधार तथा स्थानीय तहको संरचनागत बहसमा नागरिक समाजको आवाजलाई संस्थागत रूपमा समेट्न पनि निर्वाचन आयोगको ध्यानाकर्षण गराएको छ। Kathmandu. The Independent Citizens' Campaign, Nepal has demanded that the upcoming local elections be held through a non-partisan system. The campaign has submitted a memorandum to the Election Commission demanding reform of the local election system and ensuring institutional representation of civil society in all-party political dialogue. The team that reached the Commission, led by campaign chair and coordinator Rishi Dhamala, stated that a non-partisan electoral system is necessary to establish a people-oriented, transparent, and accountable governance system, keeping the local level free from partisan political interference. The campaign has stated that increasing partisanship at the local level, political polarization, problems in division and budget allocation, and deviations in public service delivery and fiscal discipline have affected the effectiveness of local governance. The memorandum urges the Commission to recommend to the government to make necessary constitutional and legal arrangements to conduct local level elections through a non-partisan system. Similarly, it is demanded to create an environment where candidates can compete freely by providing independent election symbols instead of political party election symbols in local level elections. The campaign has also demanded that the Independent Citizens' Campaign be ensured official and institutional representation in all-party political meetings, consultations, discussions, and policy debates to be organized on issues related to electoral system reform, the creation of a basic code, law amendments, and local level elections. Similarly, the campaign has also urged the government to establish the necessary legal and administrative basis for non-partisan local level elections and announce the date of the upcoming local level elections. Noting that the Constitution of Nepal 2072 BS envisages that the local level be operated on the basis of local autonomy, public participation, and direct public accountability, the campaign has emphasized the need to keep the local level free from partisan interference. The campaign has also drawn the attention of the Election Commission to institutionally include the voice of civil society in the electoral system reform and structural debate at the local level.

The Independent Citizens' Campaign, Nepal has demanded that the upcoming local elections be held through a non-partisan system. The campaign has submitted a memorandum to the Election Commission demanding reform of the local election system and ensuring institutional representation of civil society in all-party political dialogue. The team that reached the Commission, led by campaign chair and coordinator Rishi Dhamala, stated that a non-partisan electoral system is necessary to establish a people-oriented, transparent, and accountable governance system, keeping the local level free from partisan political interference. The campaign has stated that increasing partisanship at the local level, political polarization, problems in division and budget allocation, and deviations in public service delivery and fiscal discipline have affected the effectiveness of local governance. The memorandum urges the Commission to recommend to the government to make necessary constitutional and legal arrangements to conduct local level elections through a non-partisan system. Similarly, it is demanded to create an environment where candidates can compete freely by providing independent election symbols instead of political party election symbols in local level elections. The campaign has also demanded that the Independent Citizens' Campaign be ensured official and institutional representation in all-party political meetings, consultations, discussions, and policy debates to be organized on issues related to electoral system reform, the creation of a basic code, law amendments, and local level elections. Similarly, the campaign has also urged the government to establish the necessary legal and administrative basis for non-partisan local level elections and announce the date of the upcoming local level elections. Noting that the Constitution of Nepal 2072 BS envisages that the local level be operated on the basis of local autonomy, public participation, and direct public accountability, the campaign has emphasized the need to keep the local level free from partisan interference. The campaign has also drawn the attention of the Election Commission to institutionally include the voice of civil society in the electoral system reform and structural debate at the local level.

अभियानले निर्वाचन प्रणाली सुधार, आधारसंहिता निर्माण, कानुन संशोधन तथा स्थानीय तहको निर्वाचनसम्बन्धी विषयमा आयोजना हुने सर्वदलीय राजनीतिक सभा, परामर्श, छलफल र नीतिगत बहसमा स्वतन्त्र नागरिक अभियानको आधिकारिक तथा संस्थागत प्रतिनिधित्व सुनिश्चित गर्नुपर्ने मागसमेत गरेको छ।

त्यसैगरी, गैरदलीय स्थानीय तह निर्वाचनका लागि आवश्यक कानुनी तथा प्रशासनिक आधार तय गरेर आगामी स्थानीय तहको निर्वाचनको मिति घोषणा गर्न पनि अभियानले आग्रह गरेको छ।

नेपालको संविधान २०७२ ले स्थानीय तहलाई स्थानीय स्वायत्तता, जनसहभागिता र प्रत्यक्ष जनउत्तरदायित्वको आधारमा सञ्चालन गर्ने परिकल्पना गरेको उल्लेख गर्दै अभियानले स्थानीय तहलाई दलगत हस्तक्षेपबाट मुक्त राख्नुपर्नेमा जोड दिएको छ।

अभियानले निर्वाचन प्रणाली सुधार तथा स्थानीय तहको संरचनागत बहसमा नागरिक समाजको आवाजलाई संस्थागत रूपमा समेट्न पनि निर्वाचन आयोगको ध्यानाकर्षण गराएको छ।

Kathmandu. The Independent Citizens' Campaign, Nepal has demanded that the upcoming local elections be held through a non-partisan system. The campaign has submitted a memorandum to the Election Commission demanding reform of the local election system and ensuring institutional representation of civil society in all-party political dialogue. The team that reached the Commission, led by campaign chair and coordinator Rishi Dhamala, stated that a non-partisan electoral system is necessary to establish a people-oriented, transparent, and accountable governance system, keeping the local level free from partisan political interference. The campaign has stated that increasing partisanship at the local level, political polarization, problems in division and budget allocation, and deviations in public service delivery and fiscal discipline have affected the effectiveness of local governance. The memorandum urges the Commission to recommend to the government to make necessary constitutional and legal arrangements to conduct local level elections through a non-partisan system. Similarly, it is demanded to create an environment where candidates can compete freely by providing independent election symbols instead of political party election symbols in local level elections. The campaign has also demanded that the Independent Citizens' Campaign be ensured official and institutional representation in all-party political meetings, consultations, discussions, and policy debates to be organized on issues related to electoral system reform, the creation of a basic code, law amendments, and local level elections. Similarly, the campaign has also urged the government to establish the necessary legal and administrative basis for non-partisan local level elections and announce the date of the upcoming local level elections. Noting that the Constitution of Nepal 2072 BS envisages that the local level be operated on the basis of local autonomy, public participation, and direct public accountability, the campaign has emphasized the need to keep the local level free from partisan interference. The campaign has also drawn the attention of the Election Commission to institutionally include the voice of civil society in the electoral system reform and structural debate at the local level.
